summary: This bill establishes two new tax credits: one for individuals and one for businesses, to incentivize expenditures on disaster mitigation measures for homes and places of business located in areas prone to natural disasters.

scores.thoughts: This bill creates new tax credits for disaster mitigation expenditures for individuals and businesses. While tax credits reduce government revenue rather than directly increasing spending, they have a similar fiscal effect by reducing the amount of money the government collects, which can be seen as a form of indirect spending or foregone revenue. The bill does not specify any offsetting cuts or revenue increases.

The core of this bill is the creation of new tax credits for individuals and businesses that undertake disaster mitigation efforts. These credits directly reduce the tax liability for eligible taxpayers, thus lowering taxes for those who qualify and utilize the credits.

By introducing new tax credits without specifying any offsetting revenue increases or spending cuts, this bill is likely to reduce government revenue. This reduction in revenue, if not balanced, would contribute to an increase in the national debt or make debt reduction more challenging.

The bill's sole purpose is to create new nonrefundable tax credits (25% of qualified expenditures, with annual and cumulative caps) for individuals and businesses to undertake disaster mitigation. These credits reduce federal revenue with no offsets, spending cuts, or revenue raisers, directly increasing the deficit to subsidize the policy priority.
